licence.note: Refused twice over. The grant is scoped to "individual use or the use of a company for the purpose stated in your request for the data" — it presupposes a data request naming a purpose, and North Ground has made none — and redistribution is then forbidden by name: the data "may not be distributed or sold to other users without the written permission of the Commissioner". Only the Commissioner can lift this. Recorded with the geography so the ask is concrete: 40 polygon rows are 30 districts (0-29), WMD 25 being ten separate parts and WMD 26 two — parts are not districts, the trap Nova Scotia already set once. MDIFW states that where the map and the written description disagree, "the written description takes precedence". Two items a person should raise in the same letter: an undocumented WMD 0 that appears in the data but not in the published list of 29, and a Moose_Hunting_Zones layer internally named MooseZones2008 with an empty copyright field, which is NEEDS_VERIFICATION rather than usable. A Maine GeoLibrary reuse policy that search results attribute permissive language to returns 404; it is not cited and was not relied on.

geography.term: Deer Management Unit (DMU), one of 15 game geographies on one service

verifiedAgainstRegulations.detail: The service publishes geography the authority's own current regulations say no longer exists. The 2026 summary states: "Deer management units 351 and 352 have been rescinded" and "The limited firearms deer zone has been eliminated." Both DMU-351 (Mideast Upper Peninsula) and DMU-352 (Midwest Upper Peninsula unit) are still returned by the layer, stamped Year='2026' like every other row and last edited 2026-09-22, and the LimitedFirearmZoneBoundary layer is still published. Verified live 2026-09-23. Michigan's map may therefore NOT be served as the service returns it: drawing 351 or 352 would show a hunter a rescinded unit as current, and no field on the layer distinguishes them — Year does not, because it says 2026 for all 115 rows.
verifiedAgainstRegulations.consequence: Parity against the authority's own GIS service is NOT sufficient certification here, because the service is the thing that is out of date. Michigan's map lane must be certified against the REGULATIONS as well as against the service, and the rescinded units excluded by an explicit, sourced exclusion list rather than by a rule inferred from the data.

geography.alsoUnreferenced: The 2026 summary does not mention DMU-333 (Lansing core CWD area), DMU-419 (Lansing CWD management zone), DMU-486 or DMU-487 (multicounty units) or DMU-499 (Urban deer management zone) at all, though it does sell a "DMU 487 antlerless deer license". Their legal basis is therefore in the Wildlife Conservation Order rather than the summary, and is unread. This is recorded as unread, not as absent.

licence.note: A grant, stated plainly: "This dataset is a public record and … there are no restrictions on the use, reproduction, or distribution of this dataset." Use and redistribution are both permitted, which makes Michigan the first U.S. state whose geometry North Ground could lawfully store — though the owner's standing decision keeps U.S. layers live-service only, so that permission is held in reserve rather than acted on. Read on the dataset's own ArcGIS item; michigan.gov refuses automated clients, so the terms were read in the browser pane rather than by script. Two facts to carry into the build, not blockers: the Wildlife Conservation Order ch. XII written descriptions are the law and the mapped units are "condensed summaries", and the still-published LimitedFirearmZoneBoundary layer was eliminated by regulation for 2026 and must not be drawn. A point at the Lansing capitol returns THREE overlapping DMUs (033 Ingham County, 486 Southern Lower Peninsula, 333 Lansing CWD core) — a legitimate nesting of county, multicounty and disease geography, not a data conflict, and a state that will exercise overlapping-zone resolution properly.

servingDecision.reason: Michigan is NOT served, and the licence is not what blocks it — the licence is clear. The rescission of DMU 351 and DMU 352 is established as a FACT but not as an INSTRUMENT. Minutes of the adopting vote are evidence that a thing was decided; they are not the instrument that decided it. Nobody has read the repealing sentence, and there is no effective date. There is no version of serving this that is honest.

exclusionList.instrument: Wildlife Conservation Order Amendment No. 6 of 2026, as amended from the floor and adopted by the Natural Resources Commission on 2026-05-13
exclusionList.quote: Commissioner Walters motioned to amend Wildlife Conservation Order Amendment No. 6 of 2026 to rescind Deer Management Units (DMUs) 351 and 351 in the Upper Peninsula. Commissioner Fewins supported the motion. … The motion to approve the amendment passed by a vote of 6 to 1.
exclusionList.quoteNote: "351 and 351" is verbatim; the second is a source typo for 352.
exclusionList.corroboration: MDNR news release, 2026-05-15: "Deer Management Units 351 and 352 have been rescinded."
exclusionList.alsoRescinded: The limited firearms deer zone, by a separate floor motion, also 6-1.
exclusionList.effectiveDate: UNKNOWN. "Sept. 12, 2026" in the regulations summary is the Liberty Hunt opening day, not an order effective date — a plausible-wrong number that would have become our effective date had anyone been moving faster.
exclusionList.conformedTextNote: The conformed text as adopted is NOT PUBLISHED so far as we can establish: nine filename variants were probed across five 2026 NRC folders and all returned 404. Recorded as UNREAD, not as non-existent — 'we could not read it' is never 'it does not exist'. The candidate Signed_06WCO2026_Action_Edited.pdf is the right amendment number and the wrong version: it predates the meeting (ModDate 2026-04-15) and still contains sections 3.124, 12.483, 12.484, 1.2(17) and 2.1(4) unstruck.

servingDecision.neverCertifyFrom: THE CONSOLIDATED WILDLIFE CONSERVATION ORDER. WCO.pdf and every chapter PDF carry amendment history only through Am. 5 of 2026 (eff. 2026-04-08) and still contain the rescinded sections 3.124, 12.483 and 12.484 and the eliminated limited-firearms-zone definitions 1.2(17) and 2.1(4). It is the obvious document for a future agent to reach for, and certifying Michigan deer from it would reproduce exactly the defect this decision refuses to ship.

precedence.evidence: Not merely unfound — absent by drafting choice, which is a stronger finding. Across 183 pages: 'precedence' 0 hits, 'supersede' 0, 'most restrictive' 0, 'shall govern' 0, 'shall control' 0, 'overlap' 0. The single 'more restrictive … shall prevail' concerns federal versus state migratory-bird permits, not geography. Where the drafters wanted mutual exclusion they wrote it into the definitions — §12.19b defines its unit as counties 'except those lands defined in section 12.33a' — so the absence elsewhere is deliberate. Units 486, 487, 499 and 333 genuinely overlap the county units and nothing resolves them: evaluate every containing unit and return CONFLICT.

servingDecision.kindNotDerivable: A unit's kind must be assigned per Chapter XII section and stored as data, never inferred. Decisive on its own: the layer contains code 261, which does not occur anywhere in the Wildlife Conservation Order. The GIS also contradicts the Order twice — DMU-499's GIS heading says 'Urban deer management zone' while §12.499's operative sentence defines a 'January archery deer management zone', and 359's number never appears in the body of its own section. Number ranges do not encode kind either (349/351, 354/359 and 486/487/499 are different kinds within the same hundreds).
servingDecision.unitsThatGovernNothing: DMU-486 governs nothing in the Order: the string 486 occurs only inside §12.486 itself. It is a licence-administration and mapping construct. DMU-487 by contrast is a row in §3.105a Table 4, which is why an antlerless licence for it is sellable.
servingDecision.lowerPeninsulaIsCounty: CONFIRMED from the Order's own words: 'establish limits on the number of universal antlerless deer licenses that hunters could use for each deer management unit in the Upper Peninsula and each county in the Lower Peninsula.' The Order's table is literally keyed two ways — the UP column headed 'Deer Management Unit', the LP column headed 'County'. Fifteen Lower Peninsula DMUs (161, 162, 261, 262, 311, 312, 332, 341, 354, 359, 361, 452, 486, 487, 499) are not coterminous with counties, so a county-keyed limit CANNOT be resolved by DMU lookup. Michigan's Lower Peninsula cannot be answered until county geography exists, with its own licence reviewed to the same standard as any unit layer.
servingDecision.askedOfAuthority: The conformed text of WCO Amendment No. 6 of 2026 as adopted, and its effective date.

licence.note: The one state so far whose licence closes the door rather than staying silent. MNDNR grants a "personal, non-exclusive, non-transferrable, limited license" and then says the data "in its entirety may not be resold, distributed or displayed for commercial purposes or otherwise". North Ground is a commercial product, so that sentence reaches the live display as well as a stored copy: this is not a gap a person can close by reading more carefully, it is a refusal that only MNDNR can lift in writing. Recorded with the geography that would have been used so the ask is concrete. Minnesota also defines its permit areas by written road and river descriptions (Minn. R. 6232.4700, 6236.0810) and says its own map data "should not be interpreted as establishing or describing legal boundaries" — so even with permission the text, not the polygon, would be the law. Minnesota publishes no waterfowl or goose zone GIS at all; those zones are text-only and any boundary North Ground drew would be its own, never the authority's.

The State makes no warranty that the materials contained within this information are free from copyright claims or other restrictions or limitations on free use or display.
licence.note: South Dakota's permission is expressly scoped to “personal or informational use”, which does not reach a commercial product, and it speaks of the website rather than the GIS services. Separately — and this is recorded so that no one later mistakes it for a technical obstacle to solve — the deer-unit service returns 403 to an anonymous request and answers only when sent an experience.arcgis.com Referer, and its ArcGIS Online item description reads, in full, “Limit Usage in place.” That is a deliberate access control stating its own purpose. It was found and honoured: North Ground does not route around it, and a future agent must not “fix” the 403. Only three statewide archery/muzzleloader polygons are genuinely open. South Dakota's units are also defined by county in S.D. Admin. R. 41:06:21:02 (“Unit ERD-03A: Brown County, excluding Sand Lake National Wildlife Refuge”), with exclusions the GIS attributes do not carry, and the rule codes (ERD-12A) differ from the GIS UNITNO (12A). A person must ask SDGFP.

licence.note: Silence, recorded as silence. Everything WDNR publishes about this dataset is a warranty disclaimer: nothing grants commercial use, redistribution or attribution terms, and there is no CC licence, state open-data licence or public-domain dedication. The ISO 19115 metadata sets BOTH access and use constraints to "otherRestrictions" and leaves the restriction text empty — the restrictive code is on with nothing said, which is the opposite of a grant. Wisconsin is otherwise one of the easiest states to serve (units mirror county lines and NR 10.28 defines them by map rather than by text), which is exactly why the licence had to be read first.

reachability.notTheSameAsLicenceBlocked: No licence claim is made for Arizona, in either direction. The service was never read, so its terms were never read. Silence about terms is not a refusal and must not be recorded as one.

licence.statedAs: The New Mexico Department of Wildlife (NMDOW) provides spatial data as a courtesy for general location purposes only. NMDOW makes no warranty and assumes no responsibility or liability for the accuracy, timeliness, completeness, or suitability of this data for any particular use.
licence.note: Two sentences doing two different jobs. The second is a pure warranty disclaimer. The FIRST contains "as a courtesy for general location purposes only", which is a purpose limitation and may or may not be intended to restrict reuse — it is close to Maine's "for reference purposes only", which this registry already treats as RESTRICTED, but Maine's goes on to say the written description controls, and New Mexico's does not. The difference is real and not ours to resolve, so it is UNRESOLVED rather than RESTRICTED: recording it as a refusal would overstate what the publisher said.

discovery.howFound: ArcGIS Online portal search, then filtered to the authority's own account (owner keary.howley@dgf.nm.gov_nmdgf). The service's own copyrightText is EMPTY; the licence text lives on the portal ITEM, not the service, which is where it would be missed.
discovery.speciesSpecificGeography: NOT separate layers. The unit polygons carry Bear_Zone and Cougar_Zone as ATTRIBUTES, so New Mexico expresses species-specific geography as a join on the GMU rather than as a second polygon set. Anything modelling this must read the attribute rather than looking for another service.
discovery.authorityNaming: The licence text names the "New Mexico Department of Wildlife (NMDOW)" while the publishing account is @dgf.nm.gov, the Department of Game and Fish. The two names refer to the same body; which is current was not established here.

licence.statedAs: No warranty is made by the Nevada Department of Wildlife as to the accuracy, reliability, or completeness of these data for individual use or aggregate use with other data.
licence.note: The ENTIRE statement is a warranty disclaimer — 172 characters, disclaiming accuracy, reliability and completeness, and never mentioning use, reuse, redistribution or commerce. So Nevada has written terms and they do not address the question. See aWarrantyDisclaimerIsNotALicence.

discovery.howFound: ArcGIS Online portal search filtered to the authority's own account (owner riley.dunavent_NDOW). The service's copyrightText is empty; the disclaimer is on the portal item.
discovery.whichLayerIsTheGEOGRAPHY_unresolved: Nevada publishes FIVE similarly-named unit services, and choosing wrongly would be a silent error. NDOWGameMgmtUnits and NDOW_Hunt_Units both return 129 features; NDOWHuntUnitBoundaries_GroupedBounds returns 214. Nevada's regulations set some seasons by unit and others by unit GROUP, so 129 and 214 are probably both real and serve different rules. Which layer a given season is written in has NOT been established and must be read from the regulations, not guessed from a service name.
discovery.unitsAreTemporal: NDOWGameMgmtUnits carries CLOSED; NDOW_Hunt_Units carries is_open, is_active, year_activated and year_deactivated. So Nevada's unit set changes over time and a date is part of the question. A snapshot taken without the date fields would answer last year's geography for this year's hunt.
discovery.speciesApplicability: NDOWGameMgmtUnits carries Bear, Sheep, Deer and Elk as per-unit fields, so species applicability is an attribute here too, as in New Mexico.

geography.term: hunt boundary (Utah publishes one combined boundary set, not a single unit system)
geography.definedBy: the authority's own polygons, each carrying its written metes-and-bounds description in a Description field

licenceAbsent.finding: Utah's service is fully reachable and complete. What is missing is any statement of reuse terms at all — not terms that are unclear, and not terms that refuse.
whereLooked: the MapServer service's own copyrightText — EMPTY
the ArcGIS Online portal, searched for UGRC/AGRC-owned hunt items — 0 results
Utah's open-data hub full DCAT-US feed at https://opendata.gis.utah.gov/api/feed/dcat-us/1.1.json — 3.1 MB returned, 0 datasets matching "hunt"
licenceAbsent.controlForTheAbsence: The DCAT feed is a POSITIVE control: it returned 200 and 3.1 MB of datasets, so zero hunt matches is a measured absence rather than a failed request. Utah's hub does carry a site-level CC-BY-SA, which is exactly why this matters — the hub's licence would have covered a hub-published copy, and there is none.
licenceAbsent.theTrapAvoided: Utah's open-data hub advertises CC-BY-SA in its own site configuration. That governs the HUB, not dwrmapserv.utah.gov, which is the Division's own host. Applying a hub licence to a dataset published only on an agency host would be inventing a grant.
licenceAbsent.whatWouldUnblockIt: A statement of reuse terms from the Utah Division of Wildlife Resources for dwrmapserv.utah.gov, or publication of the same layer on Utah's licensed open-data hub.
licenceAbsent.whyItsOwnStateAndNotReachability: It was first recorded under `reachability` with a note saying it was not a transport problem — the exact error of rounding a source into the nearest existing field that §41A forbids. Nevada is the near neighbour and still different: Nevada HAS written terms that do not mention reuse, so its publisher has a terms process and needs a question answered. Utah's has written nothing.

discovery.howFound: The authority's own host, dwrmapserv.utah.gov, via its ArcGIS service directory rather than a portal search.
discovery.whyThisStateIsTheMostCompleteSoFar: Utah publishes geometry AND the hunt join in one place: layer 0 holds 686 named hunt boundaries, and table 1 (NRDWRGIS.%HUNT_INFO_MOBILE) holds 3,037 rows keyed BOUNDARY_NAME / BOUNDARYID / HUNT_NUMBER / SEASON. So hunt number → boundary → season is resolvable from the authority alone, which is the shape Hunt needs and is rarer than the geometry.
discovery.speciesSpecificGeography: Utah does NOT discriminate species on the boundary layer. Its BTYPE field is null or empty for almost every row — only "CWMU" is populated — so which species and class a boundary serves comes from the HUNT_NUMBER in the join table (for example DB1348), not from the polygon. Anything grouping Utah's geography by a layer attribute would find nothing.
discovery.seasonsAreNotAllPublished: Some SEASON values are not dates: "Contact CWMU Operator for 2026 season dates". Cooperative Wildlife Management Unit seasons are deferred to a private operator, so those hunts are a genuine UNKNOWN even with the join in hand and must never be rendered as a season.
discovery.writtenDescriptionsExist: Each boundary carries a written metes-and-bounds Description. Maine's precedent here is that where a written description accompanies a polygon the description may control; Utah states no precedence either way, and it has not been established.

geography.term: Hunting Area (separate mammal and bird unit designations on one polygon)
geography.definedBy: Hawaii Administrative Rules Title 13, DLNR, Subtitle 5, Part 2, Chapters 122 (Game Birds) and 123 (Game Mammals), as depicted in DOFAW's Hunting Regulation Guides

licence.statedAs: State of Hawaii Terms of Use The contents of this web page are public domain and to the extent indicated otherwise in the Terms of Use, are exempt from Terms of Use policy restrictions. There are no expressed warranties associated with the release of this data or product.
licence.attribution: State of Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources
licence.note: THE FIRST EXPRESS CLEAR LICENCE FOUND IN THE UNITED STATES. "The contents of this web page are public domain", from the Hawaii Statewide GIS Program, on the State's own host, with the layer's copyrightText naming the Department of Land and Natural Resources — the actual wildlife authority. ONE QUALIFICATION, recorded rather than waved through: the sentence qualifies itself "to the extent indicated otherwise in the Terms of Use", and that page could NOT be located — planning.hawaii.gov/gis/terms-of-use/ returns 404, and neither planning.hawaii.gov/gis/, geoportal.hawaii.gov nor portal.ehawaii.gov/page/terms-of-use/ contains the phrase. So the grant is express and its own carve-out is unverifiable. A person should resolve the cross-reference before geometry is stored.

discovery.howFound: Layer name search, then confirmed by host (geodata.hawaii.gov) and by the layer's own copyrightText.
discovery.whyThisIsTheStrongestUSFinDING: It is the only US layer found so far that cites the regulation it implements: its description names HAR Title 13 Chapters 122 and 123 and links DOFAW's published PDFs. Geometry, species applicability and the governing rule arrive together.
discovery.speciesApplicabilityIsOnThePolYGON: Fields mammal_uni and bird_unit carry SEPARATE mammal and bird unit designations, and status distinguishes them: Hunting Area (Mammal and Bird) 81, Hunting Area (Mammal ONLY) 35, Hunting Area (Bird ONLY) 5. So one polygon can be open to mammals and closed to birds, and a model that treated "hunting area" as one geography would answer the wrong species.
discovery.theLayerAlsoHoldsCLOSURES: Of 186 polygons only 121 are hunting areas. The rest are CLOSED 13, No Hunting 16, Safety Zone 19 and Safety Zone (NO HUNTING) 17. Counting the layer's feature count as a unit count would overstate Hawaii's huntable geography by 54 percent and, worse, could draw a safety zone as a hunting unit.
discovery.islands: Hawaii, Kauai, Lanai, Maui, Molokai, Oahu — all six, in an island field, which is the geography §39 asks to be treated on its own terms.

licence.statedAs: 1. The NYS DEC asks to be credited in derived products. 2. Secondary Distribution of the data is not allowed. 3. Any documentation provided is an integral part of the data set. Failure to use the documentation in conjunction with the digital data constitutes misuse of the data.
licence.attribution: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
licence.note: An EXPRESS refusal, not a silence: "Secondary Distribution of the data is not allowed." That is the clearest redistribution prohibition found in any US state, and it is decisive — serving stored geometry to a browser is distribution. Clause 1 asks to be credited in derived products, so derived products are contemplated; clause 2 still forbids passing the data on. Only a written exception from NYS DEC would change it.

discovery.howFound: Owner srvDECGISPub@srv_cld.ny.gov_nysdec — the Department's own service account.

geography.term: Wildlife Management Unit (WMU); the Oregon Administrative Rules call the same thing a "wildlife unit"
geography.definedBy: Oregon Administrative Rules chapter 635, Division 080 "WILDLIFE UNITS" — one rule per unit, 635-080-0010 (Saddle Mountain) through 635-080-0077 (Fort Rock). OAR 635-080-0000: for the purpose of managing Oregon's wildlife the State has been divided into separate described areas called wildlife units. The boundary definition is TEXTUAL; the GIS is a depiction of it, and ODFW's own licence note says so by pointing at the OAR division.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: The layer returns 69 features. 67 are managed units (REGION EAST 47, WEST 20); TWO are REGION='NOT MANAGED' — UNIT_NUM 0 'WARM SPRING INDIAN RESERVATION' and UNIT_NUM 1 'CRATER LAKE NP'. Counting 69 would overstate Oregon's unit system by two AND would draw a reservation and a national park as huntable management units. Corroborated independently: unit numbers run 10–77 with 13 absent, which is exactly 67, and matches the OAR division's per-unit rule numbering.

licence.statedAs: Boundaries may not be altered without permission of the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife. For official legal boundary description see: https://secure.sos.state.or.us/oard/displayDivisionRules.action?selectedDivision=2968
licence.attribution: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
licence.note: A restriction on ALTERATION, which is not a restriction on USE. "Boundaries may not be altered without permission" forbids changing the geometry; it says nothing about drawing it, querying it or redistributing it unchanged. So UNRESOLVED rather than RESTRICTED — classifying an alteration clause as a use refusal would be the over-strict error §8 treats as equally false. It DOES bear on §41B's simplification: a zoom-generalised copy is arguably an altered boundary, and that question is unresolved and load-bearing for how Oregon could ever be drawn.

discovery.howFound: Host nrimp.dfw.state.or.us, ODFW's own, corroborated by four separate ODFW staff accounts publishing the same 69-unit layer.
discovery.regulationsLead: The licence links the Oregon Administrative Rules division carrying the official legal boundary descriptions — a regulations source arriving inside a licence, which is unusual and worth keeping.

temporalBreak.finding: Eastern Oregon DEER changed management geography in 2026. The official artifact's "What's new for 2026" (p. 13): a shift from Wildlife Management Units to deer hunt areas, with new hunt names and numbers. ODFW's own article (https://myodfw.com/articles/eastern-oregon-deer-hunts, dated 2025-11-21) explains it: from 2026 eastern Oregon deer hunts are organized by Deer Hunt Areas instead of WMUs, built on 22 mule deer herd ranges identified from over 1,400 GPS-collared deer, renamed alphanumerically (NE-01).
temporalBreak.whyItMatters: A 2025 answer keyed to WMUs is WRONG for 2026 eastern Oregon deer, and a 2026 answer is wrong for 2025. This is a change of geographic IDENTITY, not a boundary adjustment, so no amount of reprojection reconciles them.
temporalBreak.howTheYearIsCarried: By SERVICE NAME, not by a field — the more dangerous form, because a schema check for is_active, year_deactivated or an effective date finds nothing and looks clean. No temporal field exists on any layer. 100Series_HuntBoundary_2026, 400Series_, 500Series_, 700Series_, MD_HuntAreas ("2026"), MD_HerdRanges ("2026"). Searching the owning account for 2025 equivalents returned only the 2026 set, so prior years are retired rather than kept: a stored snapshot cannot answer a past year, and a hard-coded 2026 URL will silently answer the WRONG year once ODFW publishes 2027.

speciesGeography.pattern: SEPARATE ANNUAL LAYERS, one per controlled-hunt series — not an attribute on one layer.
speciesGeography.theOneCharacterTrap: Two services differ by a single character. 100Series_HuntBoundary_2026 (singular) holds BUCK deer at layer 7, 162 features. 100Series_HuntBoundaries_2026 (plural) holds ANTLERLESS deer at layer 1, 72 features. Worse, the portal item pointing at the plural service is TITLED "600Series_HuntBoundaries_2026". Picking by service name alone silently swaps buck and antlerless geography — the same class of hazard as Nevada's.
speciesGeography.layerIdsAreNotZero: Layer ids are 7, 1, 19, 21, 3. A layer-0 assumption fails on almost all of them.
speciesGeography.classIsInTheData: The buck-deer layer's Animal field separates 'One buck with visible antler' (115), 'One mule deer buck with visible antler' (14), 'One white-tailed deer buck with visible antler' (8), 'One white-tailed deer' (8), 'One deer' (6) — so mule, white-tailed and black-tailed deer and the antlered/antlerless class are all distinguished inside one nominal species, which is §16's sex/age-versus-regulatory-class separation arriving as real data.
speciesGeography.theWMUIsOnlyTheBase: Most big-game seasons are set by controlled-hunt areas DERIVED from WMUs: "Hunt Area Entire Wildlife Management Unit unless indicated with an asterisk(*)", with textual controlled-hunt descriptions appended (pp. 94–103). The hunt-boundary layers carry UnitType = full unit (140), subunit (17), multiunit (5) and a HuntDesc field holding the authority's prose. So a coordinate resolves to a WMU, and the applicable hunt area is a full, partial or multi-WMU composite of it, per species and per year.
speciesGeography.gameBirds: No ODFW-owned GIS for waterfowl zones or upland regions was located from any _ODFW or ODFW_AGO account.

geography.definedBy: the "Washington's Big Game Hunting Seasons and Regulations" pamphlet, whose legal description the layer says takes precedence

licence.statedAs: The data set was created at a 1:100,000. Zooming in to scales finer then 1:100,000 may produce inconsistancies with the actual ground feature being represented. The feature class was created based on the "Washington's Big Game Hunting Seasons and Regulations" pamphlet. If any difference is found between the legal description for the Game Management Unit in the Pamphlet and what is represented in the feature class, the legal description language takes precedence.
licence.attribution: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
licence.note: Accuracy and PRECEDENCE, no use terms. The operative sentence is Maine's rule in Washington's words: "If any difference is found between the legal description for the Game Management Unit in the Pamphlet and what is represented in the feature class, the legal description language takes precedence." That is a statement about which artefact governs, not about reuse — so UNRESOLVED. It is also a scale limit worth heeding: created at 1:100,000, and the layer warns that finer zooms misrepresent the ground.

discovery.howFound: Host geodataservices.wdfw.wa.gov, WDFW's own, owner WDFWAdministrator.
discovery.twoLayersOneGeography: The same service exposes "GMU Generalized" at 152 features and "GMU Boundary" at 1,688. 152 is the unit count; 1,688 is boundary SEGMENTS, each attributed with the ground feature it follows. Reading 1,688 as a unit count would overstate Washington elevenfold — the same class of error as counting Hawaii's safety zones as hunting areas.

silenceIsNotRefusal: Two different states of the world are both recorded as blocked, and they are undone differently. SILENCE (UNRESOLVED) means no grant is stated either way: the publisher may simply never have been asked, so a person must ask it. A REFUSAL (RESTRICTED, or redistribution PROHIBITED) means the publisher has answered, and the answer is no: reading its terms more carefully will not change them, and only a written exception from it would. Reporting the two identically would make a refusal look like an errand.
reachabilityIsNotLicence: A source that cannot be reached SECURELY is blocked for a different reason than one whose terms refuse us, and the two must not be merged. Arizona is the first: its own GIS host has served an expired certificate since 2022, so North Ground has never been able to read its terms at all. Recording that as a licence finding would assert something about terms nobody has read; recording it as 'no source' would be false, because the authority publishes one. It is its own state, and the remedy belongs to the authority rather than to us.
aWarrantyDisclaimerIsNotALicence: Several states answer a licence question with a WARRANTY disclaimer, which is a different legal instrument: it disclaims liability for accuracy and says nothing about reuse. Nevada's whole statement is one. Reading "no warranty" as "no permission" would invent a refusal; reading it as permission would invent a grant. Both are UNRESOLVED, and the note says which kind of silence it is, because a disclaimer means the publisher HAS written terms and they simply do not address use — which is a different ask than a publisher who has written nothing.
threeWaysAFindingCanLackALicence: A finding carries exactly one of: `licence` (terms were read, whatever they say), `reachability` (the service could not be reached securely, so its terms could not be read either — Arizona), or `licenceAbsent` (the service is fine and the publisher has stated nothing — Utah). They are not interchangeable because the next action differs: read the terms, ask the authority to fix its certificate, or ask the authority to state terms at all.
